name: Cimarron National Grassland Free Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Cimarron National Grassland District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout the 108,000-acre national grassland. Must park within 30 feet of public Forest Service dirt roads.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in prairie soil, 200 feet from Cimarron River channel. Pack out all paper products.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. All trash must be packed out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood; shortgrass prairie wood gathering is non-existent.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires permitted only in containerized fire pans or established rock rings due to extreme prairie grass fire risk. Must be completely cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Strict Red Flag Warning fire bans during dry prairie wind spells.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved dirt and gravel prairie roads (FS 600 series / Cimarron River Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat dirt prairie roads. Can turn muddy and slick after rain.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible on main dirt roads during dry weather)

amenities: Santa Fe Historic National Historic Trail Access

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 60-75°F, high prairie winds (25-45 mph gusts), prairie wildflowers.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (90-100°F), intense sun, afternoon severe thunderstorm / tornado watching season.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal boondocking weather (65-80°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), clear dry skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold prairie winter (25-45°F daytime, freezing 10-25°F nights), strong blustery winds.

dangers_and_hazards: High prairie wind gusts capable of damaging RV awnings and light tents
Prairie wildfire risk during Red Flag Warnings
Severe thunderstorm and hail / tornado risk during late spring/early summer
Prairie Rattlesnakes active in warm months

common_human_made_sounds: Distant freight train horn on Santa Fe railroad line (6 miles away)
Wind blowing through tall prairie grasses

human_demographics_and_culture: Santa Fe Trail history enthusiasts, solar digital nomads, birdwatchers, and long-distance overland rigs.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Comanche and Kiowa indigenous traditions honor the vast open plains of the Cimarron River basin as sacred domains of the wind spirits and buffalo guardians.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Infinite horizon energy, profound spatial freedom, 100% uninterrupted solar panel charging.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Santa Fe National Historic Trail (Cimarron Route)
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Historic wagon ruts from 19th-century Santa Fe Trail traders

public_reviews_summary: Incredible wide-open prairie boondocking location with zero crowds and excellent cell signal. Solar power generation is 100% effortless.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 dark sky. Endless prairie views.

name: Cimarron National Grassland Dispersed Primitive Zone

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Cimarron National Grassland

rules_and_regulations.cost: Free ($0/night, no fee for primitive dispersed grassland camping)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed camping allowed across 108,000 acres of shortgrass prairie outside developed areas. Maintain 100 feet distance from water tanks and windmills.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Bury human waste 6-8 inches deep in cat-holes at least 200 feet from Cimarron River and windmills.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Dead and down wood collection permitted along river bottom cottonwoods.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Clear ground 10 feet around campfire. Extinguish thoroughly with water due to high prairie wind hazard.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Subject to USFS high prairie fire danger restrictions.

access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat gravel roads; sandy dirt spur roads can become muddy after rain.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Standard FWD car fine on main gravel roads; 4WD recommended for sandy river bed spurs.

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: Vast prairie winds and spring blooming yucca.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot high plains weather (90-100°F) with intense sun and cool prairie nights.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Crisp, clear autumn days with golden shortgrass plains.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold, windy high plains winter (15-35°F) with periodic blizzards.

dangers_and_hazards: High Prairie Winds & Rapid Wildfire Spread
human_demographics_and_culture: High Plains pioneer and Santa Fe Trail historic trading heritage.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Pioneer history recalls Point of Rocks as a crucial landmark guide along the arid Cimarron Cutoff of the Santa Fe Trail.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: 360-degree prairie horizons create a humbling sense of cosmic expanse.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Santa Fe Companion National Historic Trail
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Historic 1800s wagon ruts, Point of Rocks overlook, prairie wildlife

public_reviews_summary: Vast open shortgrass prairie with mind-blowing starry night skies, but high winds and hot sun require full prep.
other_data: Bring plenty of fresh water and check fire danger ratings before lighting any camp stove.
